title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.

title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing identify emodin as a candidate modulator of STAT3 signaling in abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node. Subsequent functional studies demonstrated that emodin suppressed vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching, and inflammatory responses. These effects were accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. Molecular docking suggested a potential binding mode of emodin within the STAT3 SH2 domain, while cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated thermal stabilization of STAT3 by emodin in intact cells, consistent with target engagement. Notably, emodin and the selective STAT3 inhibitor STAT3-IN-13 produced comparable effects, and co-treatment did not yield additive efficacy, suggesting overlapping mechanisms. In vivo, emodin attenuated aneurysm development and reduced vascular inflammation in experimental models. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a candidate modulator of AAA progression acting through suppression of STAT3-associated signaling pathways, and demonstrate the potential of genetic evidence-guided drug repurposing strategies in complex vascular diseases.

title: Effect of Extended-Duration Venous Thromboprophylaxis After Cancer Surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer patients undergoing surgery are at significantly increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Although extended thromboprophylaxis is recommended, the optimal anticoagulant type and duration remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of different extended thromboprophylaxis in this population. METHODS: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed to evaluate various thromboprophylaxis strategies for patients undergoing cancer-related surgery. We conducted both three-node and five-node network analyses to evaluate extended-duration versus standard-duration thromboprophylaxis strategies. Outcomes included venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. Net clinical benefit and risk-benefit assessments were additionally performed to determine the overall impact of prolonged anticoagulant therapy. Treatment effects were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs). RESULTS: A total of 14 randomized controlled trials involving 4,331 participants were included. Compared with placebo, extended-duration prophylaxis with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) (RR 0.12, 95% CrI 0.05-0.27) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) (RR 0.17, 95% CrI 0.05-0.55) significantly reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism without a corresponding increase in major bleeding. In net clinical benefit analyses, both prolonged DOAC therapy (RR 0.27, 95% CrI 0.14-0.49) and LMWH (RR 0.36, 95% CrI 0.17-0.76) demonstrated favorable overall outcomes. Risk-benefit evaluation suggested that prolonged DOACs provided a more advantageous balance than LMWH, with an NNH/NNT ratio of 4.17. CONCLUSIONS: Extended thromboprophylaxis is effective and safe for cancer patients undergoing surgery. Besides, DOACs appears to be the optimal anticoagulant for extended thromboprophylaxis, providing the greatest net clinical benefit.

title: Characterizing the Thrombotic Spectrum and Clinical Phenotypes of Tranexamic Acid-Associated Adverse Events: A Pharmacovigilance Study Based on the FAERS Database.
abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in surgical, trauma, obstetric, and gynecological settings. However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Thrombotic adverse events were identified using the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "Embolic and thrombotic events" and evaluated by disproportionality analysis based on reporting odds ratios (RORs). Qualifying thrombotic events were assigned to the SMQ vessel-type subgroups-arterial, vessel-type unspecified/mixed, and venous-and demographic characteristics, indications, clinical outcomes and time-to-onset were compared across subgroups; signal strength was further related to clinical severity. In all, 515 thrombotic cases associated with TXA and 26 selected thrombotic terms were found (arterial, 157; mixed, 168; venous, 190). Venous thromboembolism-pulmonary embolism (n = 128, ROR 13.94) and deep vein thrombosis (n = 58, ROR 9.09)-is the most frequent type and brings about the most severe and fatal consequences (death reported in 16.8% of venous versus 2.5% of arterial reports), whereas the strongest disproportionality signals were observed for rare site-specific events such as ovarian vein thrombosis (ROR 352.95) and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (ROR 118.35). The three subgroups differed markedly in demographic and clinical characteristics: venous events occurred predominantly in women (73.7%) treated for menorrhagia (35.3%), whereas arterial events arose mainly in surgical or procedural settings (intravenous route 36.3%; surgery/prophylaxis 19.1%) and presented earliest after exposure [median time-to-onset (TTO) 0 versus 7 days]. Signal strength was not concordant with clinical severity across the thrombotic spectrum. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the thrombotic safety of TXA, indicate that the clinical background may influence the phenotypic differences among the different thrombotic types, and emphasize the necessity of enhanced attention and risk stratification in high-risk groups.

title: Association between thyroid feedback quantile-based index and the risk of in-hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer.
abstract: AIMS: To investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback quantile-based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU). METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles. Model 1 was unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and smoking; Model 3 additionally adjusted for diabetes duration, HbA1c, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, CRP, and dyslipidemia. RCS assessed dose-response patterns; Firth regression was used for sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Fifty-six patients underwent amputation. In Model 3, each 1-SD increase in TFQI (equivalent to a 1-unit increase in pre-scaled TFQI) was associated with higher odds of amputation (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.63-3.15; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, ORs were 2.94 (0.98-8.83; P = 0.055), 5.60 (1.88-16.67; P = 0.002), and 14.79 (5.22-41.89; P < 0.001) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS showed an overall association (P = 0.002) and nonlinearity (P = 0.046) in Model 3. Firth estimates were broadly consistent with conventional regression. CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized DFU patients with normal thyroid function, higher TFQI levels are associated with an increased risk of amputation during hospitalization. Nevertheless, the clinical utility of TFQI requires further validation in prospective studies.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyses were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p=0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: P P Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21];=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (for noninferiority=0.004). title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: Quantitative assessment of foot microcirculation by CT perfusion differentiates chronic limb-threatening ischemia from claudication in peripheral artery disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is validated to assess foot microcirculatory perfusion in peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study aimed to investigate differences in foot microcirculation on CTP between patients with claudication (Cla) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and to develop diagnostic models for CLTI. METHODS: This single-center prospective study enrolled hospitalized patients with PAD at Huadong Hospital, China (October 2022 to January 2024). Participants underwent preoperative foot CTP and were stratified into Cla (Rutherford category 3) and CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) groups. Baseline characteristics and perfusion parameters were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed. RESULTS: p p p p A total of 57 patients with PAD were included (34 Cla, 23 CLTI). Resting ankle-brachial index and Global Limb Anatomic Staging System scores did not differ significantly between groups. Diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence was higher in the CLTI group (95.7% vs 52.9%;= 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression identified hemoglobin (Hb) level (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.822-0.986;= 0.024), time to peak (TTP) (OR, 1.135; 95% CI, 1.045-1.250;= 0.003), and blood flow (BF) (OR, 0.668; 95% CI, 0.499-0.894;= 0.007) as independent predictors for CLTI. Four diagnostic models were constructed: model A (BF + DM, area under the curve [AUC] 0.864), model B (BF + Hb, AUC 0.890), model C (TTP + DM, AUC 0.895), and model D (TTP + Hb, AUC 0.874). title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.
abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.

title: Taohong Siwu Decoction-Based Targeted Drug Penetration Therapy for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Hip Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Postoperative lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a common complication after hip fracture surgery, and complementary strategies targeting coagulation, inflammation, and venous circulation may provide additional preventive benefits. This retrospective cohort study included 86 patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between June 2023 and June 2024. Patients were assigned to a control group (n = 43), receiving standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis, or an observation group (n = 43), receiving additional Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy. The primary outcome was postoperative lower limb DVT within 10 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes included coagulation parameters, inflammatory markers, femoral venous blood flow velocities, postoperative pain, limb swelling, and treatment-related adverse events. DVT occurred in 1/43 patients (2.33%) in the observation group and 10/43 patients (23.26%) in the control group (Fisher's exact P = 0.007). In a parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression model adjusting for age and baseline D-dimer, adjunctive therapy remained associated with a lower likelihood of postoperative DVT (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.68, P = 0.017). After 10 days of treatment, the observation group had lower Faces Pain Scale-Revised scores and limb swelling, longer activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time, lower D-dimer levels, higher common and superficial femoral vein blood flow velocities, and lower serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-6 levels than the control group (all P < 0.05). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in overall adverse-event occurrence, and no severe treatment-related adverse events were recorded. Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy combined with standard anticoagulation was associated with a lower incidence of early postoperative DVT and favorable differences in coagulation, inflammatory, and venous hemodynamic parameters.

title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD. METHODS: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy. RESULTS: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents. CONCLUSION: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae RkMsn4, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates carotenoid and lipid metabolism to enhance tolerance to environmental stress in.
abstract: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Red yeasts serve as indispensable microbial resources for the production of carotenoids and lipids; however, environmental stress factors often limit their performance during industrial fermentation. The zinc-finger transcription factors Msn2/Msn4 act as central regulators of stress responses in yeasts. However, researchers have not yet systematically elucidated the similarities and differences in the mechanisms underlying the regulatory effects of Msn2/Msn4 under different stress conditions. In this study, we compared the shared and stress-specific regulatory functions of RkMsn4 inYM25235 under conditions of glucose starvation, 15 °C low temperature, and 4% NaCl salt stress. RkMsn4 contributed to the activity of the oxidative defense systems, including antioxidant enzymes, carotenoids, and glutathione, and the remodeling of membrane lipids, including phospholipids and unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs) across all three stress conditions. Additionally, RkMsn4 regulated stress-specific metabolic regulation by modulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and aromatic amino acid (AAA) metabolism under glucose starvation conditions and promoting the utilization of exogenous sucrose and fructose under salt stress. By conducting weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified candidate genes potentially associated with carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide practical insights for improving tolerance to stress and metabolic productivity of red yeasts in industrial bioprocesses.IMPORTANCERed yeasts are important microorganisms for the production of carotenoids and lipids, but their performance is often limited by environmental stress. Understanding how red yeasts respond to environmental stress is crucial for advancing their application in industrial fermentation. This study reveals the stress response mechanisms mediated by the transcription factor RkMsn4 inYM25235 under glucose starvation, low temperature, and salt stress, as well as its regulatory role in carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the stress resistance and productivity of red yeasts in industrial applications.

title: Hybrid pin penetration open stent technique: Retrospective study of a new approach to frozen elephant trunk procedure.
abstract: Total arch replacement using the frozen elephant trunk technique for acute type A aortic dissection involving the aortic arch remains technically demanding because of complex supra-aortic branch reconstruction and prolonged circulatory arrest. We developed a modified fenestrated open stent technique, termed the hybrid pin-penetration open stent (HIPPOS) technique, to simplify branch reconstruction while minimizing supra-aortic vessel manipulation. We retrospectively reviewed 15 consecutive patients who underwent total arch replacement using HIPPOS between May 2024 and May 2026 at a single institution by a single surgeon. Following deployment of a Frozenix open stent graft (Japan Lifeline), antegrade fenestrations were created under direct vision using needle penetration and sequential dilation, followed by reconstruction with balloon-expandable covered stent grafts. All procedures were successfully completed. Operative durations decreased with increasing numbers of fenestrations, reflecting procedural refinement and the surgical learning curve. Two perioperative deaths occurred in patients with profound preoperative shock, and one patient experienced a nondisabling stroke. No postoperative hoarseness, paraplegia, fenestration-related endoleak, or distal stent-induced new entry was observed. Follow-up computed tomography angiography confirmed satisfactory graft conformability and durable branch patency. HIPPOS is a reproducible modification of the frozen elephant trunk procedure with encouraging early clinical outcomes.

title: Self-Amplifying AIE Probe for HClO-Activatable Imaging and Antioxidative/Anti-Inflammatory Therapy of Thoracic Aortic Dissection.
abstract: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular disease, yet its accurate diagnosis and effective treatment remain challenging due to poor imaging contrast and insufficient specificity. Leveraging the overexpressed reactive oxygen species (ROS) in TAD, we reported a hypochlorous acid (HClO)-activatable molecular probe DT-PZ. It enables two-stage self-amplifying fluorescence imaging (chemical activation and then physical aggregation) and light-independent therapy on a single chemical entity. The probe initially exhibits quenched fluorescence via photoinduced electron transfer (PET). Two pathways can turn on the fluorescence via chemical activation: (1) oxidation by HClO blocks PET and turns on the emission; (2) photo-triggered radicals generation of HClO (via chloride ions or myeloperoxidase) to activate neighboring probes, creating self-amplifying fluorescence. Upon accumulation at the lesion site, the physical aggregation caused by the aggregation-induced emission effect further amplifies the fluorescence signals. This two-stage fluorescence amplification mechanism enables TAD visualization within 2 min in vivo. For therapy, the phenothiazine scavenges excess ROS during non-illuminated periods, down-regulates the NF-κB/P65 signal pathway, and up-regulates eNOS and P-Akt expressions, protecting endothelial homeostasis and then improving murine survival from 50% to 90%. Collectively, DT-PZ synergizes self-amplifying fluorescence imaging with light-independent antioxidation/anti-inflammatory therapy, holding great promise for managing deep-seated cardiovascular diseases.

title: Machine learning-derived serum carbon dioxide trajectories in predicting prognosis of patients with acute aortic dissection.
abstract: Venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO 2 ) indicates postoperative adverse outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection, and its trajectories over time affecting postoperative adverse outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PvCO 2 trajectories and postoperative adverse outcomes, as well as clinical application through group-based trajectory modeling and machine-learning algorithms. This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 642 patients with acute aortic dissection treated at the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University from 2019 to 2024, to determine postoperative adverse outcomes, including 6-month mortality and complications. Three PvCO 2 tests within the first 72 hours of admission were used to analyze PvCO 2 trajectories through group-based trajectory modeling. To diagnose high-risk PvCO 2 trajectories in emergency settings, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was conducted to select key features, which were consequently integrated into predictive models using multiple machine-learning methods. Finally, a web-based interpretable website was developed for predicting PvCO 2 trajectories in patients with acute aortic dissection. Overall, 642 patients were classed into four PvCO 2 trajectories (T1, persistent decrease from a medium to a low level; T2, stable low level; T3, persistent decrease from a high to a low level; T4, stable midlevel), showing distinct patterns. After adjustment for other covariates, postoperative adverse outcomes among these groups showed significant differences, with a higher proportion of postoperative adverse outcomes in the T3 group. Subsequently, upon Shapley additive explanations analysis, 17 features with importance sequence were identified (hemoglobin, direct bilirubin, monocyte, adenosine deaminase, drinking, anion gap, chloride, platelet, lymphocyte, albumin/globulin ratio, calcium, alanine aminotransferase, α-L-fucosidase, D-dimer, antihypertensive drugs, and smoking), which were integrated into the model for predicting T3. The optimal machine-learning model was established for predicting postoperative adverse outcomes. Finally, a web-based interpretable model was developed to predict patients with acute aortic dissection and high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes. This study uncovers heterogeneity in PvCO 2 trajectory, highlighting that decreased PvCO 2 is associated with worse prognosis. A web-based tool for the prediction of acute aortic dissection patients at high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes was constructed to facilitate clinical application.

title: Risk Factors for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Surgery in Patients with Gastric or Colorectal Cancer Receiving Anticoagulant Prophylaxis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to identify perioperative predictors of early postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients undergoing surgery for gastric or colorectal cancer who received routine pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis and to develop a nomogram for postoperative risk stratification. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with gastric or colorectal cancer undergoing surgery from December 2020 to October 2023. All received postoperative low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis, and DVT was screened by ultrasonography on postoperative day 3. Predictors were identified by logistic regression and incorporated into a nomogram. RESULTS: A total of 388 eligible patients were included, among whom 124 (32.0%) had screening-detected postoperative lower-extremity DVT. Among patients with DVT, 118 (95.2%) had distal-only DVT and 114 (91.9%) were asymptomatic. Multivariable logistic regression identified age, activated partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, and postoperative day 1 D-dimer as independent predictors of postoperative DVT. The nomogram showed acceptable discrimination, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.787 (95% confidence interval 0.731-0.844) in the training cohort and 0.854 (95% confidence interval 0.774-0.934) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed risks. In decision curve analysis, the nomogram provided greater net benefit for risk classification than strategies classifying all or no patients as high risk. CONCLUSION: Age, activated partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, and postoperative day 1 D-dimer were independently associated with screening-detected early postoperative DVT. The resulting nomogram may help postoperative risk stratification and closer surveillance; however, external validation is required before routine clinical application.

title: Factors associated with patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The factors influencing patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting remain incompletely understood. We therefore conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the available evidence. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched to December 2025. Studies reporting associations between potential risk factors and stent outcomes were included. Data were synthesized narratively, and random-effects meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed when comparable multivariable-adjusted estimates were available. RESULTS: A total of 49 studies were included, predominantly involving retrospective cohorts. The meta-analysis suggested that post-thrombotic disease, stent extension across or below the inguinal ligament, and hyperlipidemia were associated with an increased risk of patency loss, whereas increasing age showed a modest inverse association with patency loss. The narrative evidence suggested that greater anatomical disease extent was associated with poorer stent patency, whereas the evidence regarding impaired venous inflow was heterogeneous and varied according to the disease phenotype, anatomical segment, and inflow definition. Pooled analyses did not identify statistically significant associations of sex, stent length, or number of stents with patency loss. Evidence regarding anticoagulation discontinuation and adjunctive antiplatelet therapy was insufficient and inconsistent. CONCLUSIONS: Patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting appears to be associated with the disease phenotype, higher anatomical disease burden, and stent landing strategy. Venous inflow impairment may also be associated with poorer stent patency, although the evidence was heterogeneous. The predominantly retrospective evidence precludes causal inference. Prospective studies with standardized definitions and robust adjustment are needed to improve risk stratification and optimize post-stenting management.

We therefore conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the available evidence. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched to December 2025.

title: Key factors for predicting outcomes one year after Meso-Rex bypass surgery and optimizing the surgical plan in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To analyze the factors for predicting 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for Meso-Rex bypass (MRB) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2014 to July 2024, children with EHPVO after MRB were retrospectively analyzed. The number of MRB, the type of bypass vessel, and the position of the lower anastomosis were collected. Predictive variables include the diameter of the connection between the left and right portal veins, the Rex vein (RV) diameter, the number of RV branches, the diameter of the thickest RV branch, and the bypass-to-superior mesenteric vein (SMV) angle, which were measured by Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) one week after MRB. The upper and lower anastomotic stenosis were diagnosed by Ultrasound and CECT one year after MRB. RESULTS: A total of 153 children (median age 72 months, 87 males) were included in this study. Univariate factors include the number of MRBs, the type of bypass vessel, and CECT variables (except the diameter of the thickest RV branch). Numbers of MRB and RV branches were retained in the final model for upper anastomotic stenosis. The combination of MRB > 1 and RV branches ≤ 4 predicts it post-MRB with 75% sensitivity, 86.4% specificity, and an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The bypass-to-SMV angle ≤ 110° predicts lower anastomotic stenosis after MRB with 90% sensitivity, 73.39% specificity, and AUC 0.847. CONCLUSIONS: Associated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the type of bypass vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle could be used to inform future surgical technique refinement. FindingsAssociated factors include bypass-to-SMV angle, number of MRB, RV branches and diameter, left-right portal vein connection diameter, and type of bypass vessel. Clinical RelevanceAssociated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the internal jugular vein as the bridge vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle > 110° could be used to optimize the surgical plan for a better outcome.

title: Adjunctive citrus flavonoids after endovenous microwave ablation for great saphenous vein varicosis: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adjunctive citrus flavonoids are associated with improved venous hemodynamics and short-term outcomes after endovenous microwave ablation (EMA) for great saphenous vein varicosis in a retrospective cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 254 patients with great saphenous vein varicosis treated between January 2022 and July 2025. Patients were grouped according to the actual treatment received: EMA alone (n = 126) or EMA plus micronized purified flavonoid fraction (MPFF; n = 128). In the combination group, MPFF was administered at 1000 mg twice daily (2000 mg/d) for 2 weeks; this was twice the usual approved dose for venolymphatic insufficiency. The primary outcome was overall clinical response at 2 weeks. Secondary outcomes included Venous Clinical Severity Score, Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire, Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire, venous hemodynamic parameters, exploratory endothelial biomarkers (such as endothelin-1, nitric oxide, and circulating endothelial cells), treatment-related adverse events, and 6-month ultrasound findings. RESULTS: Compared with EMA alone, adjunctive MPFF was associated with a higher overall clinical response and greater improvements in Venous Clinical Severity Score, Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire, and Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire scores (all P < .05). Mean and peak venous flow velocities improved more in the combination group (P < .05). The combination group also showed lower endothelin-1 and circulating endothelial cell levels and higher nitric oxide levels after treatment (P < .05). Recorded adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (P > .05). At 6 months, the combination group showed a higher rate of complete occlusion and less residual reflux (P < .05). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, adjunctive citrus flavonoids after EMA were associated with better early symptom scores, venous hemodynamic indices, and endothelial biomarker profiles without a detected increase in recorded adverse events. As the study was observational and used a nonstandard MPFF dose, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality, proof of safety, or support for the 2000 mg/d regimen. Prospective randomized trials using approved dosing are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Open- versus closed-cell stents in transfemoral carotid artery stenting for carotid bifurcation disease: a target trial emulation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The comparative association of open-cell stent (OCS) and closed-cell stent (CCS) design with outcomes after protected transfemoral carotid artery stenting, particularly long-term patency, remains uncertain. This study compared OCSs and CCSs in patients with carotid bifurcation disease. METHODS: We retrospectively emulated a target trial using data from three centers. Consecutive patients who underwent transfemoral carotid artery stenting with embolic protection devices for atherosclerotic carotid bifurcation lesions were included and classified according to stent design. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Periprocedural outcomes were assessed within 30 days. Follow-up outcomes included in-stent restenosis (ISR), severe ISR, symptomatic ISR, recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (stroke or transient ischemic attack), and target-vessel revascularization. RESULTS: Among 1024 patients, 524 (51.2%) were symptomatic and 500 (48.8%) were asymptomatic; 577 received OCSs and 447 received CCSs. Median follow-up was 26.0 months (interquartile range, 19.4-32.4 months). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, baseline covariates were well balanced. Periprocedural adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. During follow-up, CCS use was associated with higher risks of ISR (hazard ratio [HR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.19-2.31; P = .003), severe ISR (HR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.06-2.45; P = .026), symptomatic ISR (HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.20-3.45; P = .008), and recurrent transient ischemic attack (HR, 3.06; 95% CI, 1.24-7.55; P = .015). Any ISR and severe ISR were strongly associated with recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (both P < .001). CCS use appeared more strongly associated with ISR in symptomatic patients, without significant interaction by symptom status (P for interaction = .206). Sensitivity analyses were concordant with the primary results. CONCLUSIONS: OCSs were associated with a lower hazard of restenosis and no material difference in periprocedural outcomes compared with CCSs. These findings support preferential consideration of OCSs at the carotid bifurcation for long-term patency, whereas CCSs may retain a theoretical advantage in unstable plaques requiring denser plaque coverage.

title: Endovascular reintervention versus conservative medical therapy for persistent or recurrent venous-origin chronic pelvic pain after primary ovarian vein embolization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate and compare the clinical effectiveness of endovascular reintervention vs conservative medical therapy in patients with persistent or recurrent venous-origin chronic pelvic pain (CPP) after initial endovascular embolization for pelvic venous disorders (PeVDs). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 79 patients with pelvic venous disorder and persistent or recurrent venous-origin CPP following primary ovarian vein embolization who subsequently received either reintervention (n = 40) or conservative medical therapy with venoactive drugs (n = 39). The primary endpoint was the 3-month CPP relief rate [Visual Analog Scale (VAS) reduction ≥2]. Secondary endpoints included longitudinal VAS score trajectories over 12 months. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline covariates, and outcomes were analyzed using weighted logistic regression and Linear Mixed-Effects Models. RESULTS: The 3-month CPP relief rate was 67.50% (27/40) in the reintervention group and 35.90% (14/39) in the medical therapy group. After adjustment, reintervention group demonstrated significant overall superiority, with a more than threefold increase in the odds of 3-month CPP relief compared with medical therapy (odds ratio, 3.03; 95% confidence interval, 1.19-7.68; P = .022). The therapeutic advantage of reintervention was sustained through 12 months, with a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Subgroup analyses showed no significant interactions for the 3-month CPP relief. However, significant interactions were observed for 12-month VAS improvement, with greater benefit from reintervention among patients initially treated at external institutions (P < .001) and those presenting with recurrence or partial relief (P < .001). No major procedure-related complications were observed during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular reintervention-based strategy is an effective option for persistent or recurrent venous-origin CPP after initial embolization. However, therapeutic benefit varies across patient subgroups, highlighting the importance of individualized patient selection.

title: Association between intrinsic capacity, genetic predisposition, and risk of venous thromboembolism.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Association between intrinsic capacity (IC) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains unclear, we aim to explore the relationship among IC, genetic predisposition, and incident VTE. METHODS: In this large retrospective cohort study using the UK Biobank, IC, defined as the composite of all physical and mental capacities of an individual, was assessed across 7 factors (such as exhaustion, sleep duration, eye problems, hearing difficulty, weight loss, gait speed, and grip strength) and scored from 0 (best) to 7 (worst). Participants were grouped into five IC categories: 0, 1, 2, 3, and ≥4 factors. Incident VTE was identified through national medical records. Genetic predisposition to VTE was determined by the tertiles of polygenic risk score (PRS) derived from external genome-wide association data from the UK Biobank. Cox proportional hazards models were used to investigate the associations with multiple variables adjusted. RESULTS: A total of 415,581 participants (median age, 57.0 years; interquartile range, 50.0-63.0; 54.96% female; 94.89% White) were included in the final analysis. Over a median follow-up of 14.37 years, 8299 (2.00%) developed VTE, including 3878 (0.94%) with and 4421 (1.07%) without a history of cancer. Higher IC scores were associated with increased VTE risk compared to those with IC = 0 (for IC = 1: hazard ratio (HR), 1.08; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.16; P = .029; for IC = 2: HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.04-1.22; P = .005; for IC = 3: HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.06-1.34; P = .003; for IC ≥ 4: HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.23-1.75; P < .001). Similar associations were observed in both cancer and noncancer subgroups. Furthermore, individuals with both the highest PRS and the worst IC (≥4 factors) had the greatest VTE risk, with significant interactions between PRS and IC. CONCLUSIONS: Our large-scale study suggests that poor IC is an independent risk factor for VTE. Moreover, integrating IC with genetic risk can identify a high-risk subgroup, which supports the clinical utility of IC assessment in VTE risk stratification.

title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Risk for Thromboembolic Complication Among Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and thromboembolic events among women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching. SETTING: Multicenter electronic health record database (TriNetX US Collaborative Network). POPULATION: Women aged 18-45 years with a diagnosis of PCOS between 2012 and 2021. METHODS: Women with PCOS were stratified according to subsequent diagnosis of OSA and matched 1:1 with PCOS patients without OSA using propensity scores. Incident pulmonary embolism (PE) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurring after a 1-year reference period were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident pulmonary embolism and venous thromboembolism. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 20 052 women were included (10 026 per group). All analyses were conducted within this propensity score-matched cohort. PE incidence was higher among women with OSA compared with those without OSA (2.88 vs. 1.48 per 1000 person-years; absolute difference 1.40 per 1000 person-years; incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.94, 95% CI 1.49-2.53; hazard ratio [HR] 1.95, 95% CI 1.50-2.54). VTE incidence was also increased (3.74 vs. 2.87 per 1000 person-years; absolute difference 0.87 per 1000 person-years; IRR 1.30, 95% CI 1.06-1.60; HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.07-1.61). These associations persisted across clinically relevant subgroups and increased over long-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Among women with PCOS, comorbid OSA is associated with an increased risk of thromboembolic events, particularly pulmonary embolism. These findings support consideration of OSA screening and enhanced thromboembolic risk assessment in women with PCOS.

title: NDUFAF2 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm formation through mitochondrial dysfunction-induced apoptosis.
abstract: in vitro In vivo 2 Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Here, we found that NDUFAF2 (NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) 1 alpha subcomplex assembly factor 2) was significantly upregulated in cultured cells and murine AAA tissues. Knockdown of NDUFAF2attenuated Ang II-induced mitochondrial fragmentation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and apoptosis in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), while improving mitochondrial membrane potential and oxygen consumption rate. In addition, NDUFAF2 knockdown reduced the expression of DRP1 (dynamin-related protein 1) while restoring the mitochondrial fusion protein OPA1 (optic atrophy 1), and OPA1 overexpression further enhanced mitochondrial integrity and function., NDUFAF2 knockdown suppressed CaCl-induced AAA formation, preserved aortic structure, reduced apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial complex subunits and smooth muscle cell markers. These results indicate that NDUFAF2 contributes to AAA progression by triggering mitochondrial damage and apoptosis, representing a promising therapeutic target for AAA.

title: Soft robotic devices for cardiovascular medicine.
abstract: Conventional, rigid simulators and therapeutic devices for cardiovascular disease have several fundamental limitations, such as poor biomimetic fidelity, substantial surgical invasiveness and mismatch at the tissue-device interface. Soft robotic devices, with tissue-like materials, structures and functions, are emerging as promising alternatives. In this Review, by matching clinical demands to technological breakthroughs, we identify three emerging complementary frontiers in which soft robotic devices are redefining cardiovascular medicine - soft robotic simulators, such as in vitro ventricular simulators and in vivo assistive simulators; soft robotic interventional instruments, such as percutaneous instruments, endovascular continuum instruments and untethered mini-scale robots; and soft robotic implants for vascular disease, arrhythmia and heart failure. We describe the unique advantages of soft robotic devices as well as their applicable scope and technical implementation. Finally, we highlight promising technological opportunities for next-generation soft cardiac devices, evaluate the clinical maturity of existing devices and propose a translational roadmap for the coming decade. With this Review, we aim to foster further integration of soft robotics into cardiovascular medicine by identifying device solutions with translational potential to address unmet clinical needs.
